# 192 · A quote handed back as a copy with the same values, refuted on identity alone

[← All examples](../README.md)

| Verdict | Categories | Severity if shipped | Change | Verified unit | Approach |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **✗ Violation: counterexample found** | functional | medium | refactor, behaviour change not intended | [`Pricing#withQuantity`](../../examples/apps/shop/src/main/java/shop/Pricing.java) | [B9: Regression verification](../../lib/README.md) |

> The value-object refactor of 190, with `withQuantity` handing back a copy of the quote, for every quantity, instead of the quote it changed. Every field agrees with what 190 hands back; a caller that keeps the quote it passed and the one it got back sees two objects where it saw one. The tool holds the method to `result == q` within each version and refutes it on that alone, the witness replayed on the JVM with the objects' identities.

Tags: [payments](../README.md#tag-payments), [aliasing](../README.md#tag-aliasing), [joint-run](../README.md#tag-joint-run), [object-inputs](../README.md#tag-object-inputs), [own-checker](../README.md#tag-own-checker)

## The change

`Quote`'s amount, a `long` of cents, becomes a value object, `Money`, so `Quote(long cents, int quantity)` is now `Quote(Money amount, int quantity)`; `Pricing.total` reads `q.amount.cents()` where it read `q.cents`; the pure helper `Pricing.discount` (a tenth off ten items or more) is rewritten as an early return; and the route `POST /quotes` makes the quote with `new Money(cents)`. Nothing is meant to change: not the total, not the event the route sends, not what `Pricing.withQuantity` hands back. In this version `withQuantity` also makes a new quote for one item from `q`'s amount, gives it the quantity, and returns it, after setting `q`'s quantity as before.

**Before** ([`Pricing.java`](../../examples/apps/shop/src/main/java/shop/Pricing.java), line 1):

```java
package shop;

/** The pricing kernel. */
public final class Pricing {
    private Pricing() {}

    /** A tenth off an order of ten items or more. */
    static long discount(long gross, int quantity) {
        return quantity >= 10 ? gross / 10 : 0;
    }

    public static long total(Quote q) {
        long gross = q.cents * q.quantity;
        return gross - discount(gross, q.quantity);
    }

    /** The same quote for another quantity: changed in place and handed back. */
    public static Quote withQuantity(Quote q, int quantity) {
        q.quantity = quantity;
        return q;
    }
}
```

**After:**

```java
package shop;

/** The pricing kernel, over money. */
public final class Pricing {
    private Pricing() {}

    /** A tenth off an order of ten items or more, written the other way round: the changed pure helper. */
    static long discount(long gross, int quantity) {
        if (quantity < 10) return 0;
        return gross / 10;
    }

    public static long total(Quote q) {
        long gross = q.amount.cents() * q.quantity;
        return gross - discount(gross, q.quantity);
    }

    /** The same quote for another quantity: changed in place and handed back. */
    public static Quote withQuantity(Quote q, int quantity) {
        q.quantity = quantity;
        // The copy is made for one item and then given the quantity, so that it agrees with q in every field for
        // every quantity, the constructor's refusal of a quantity below 1 included: identity is all that tells them
        // apart.
        Quote copy = new Quote(q.amount, 1);
        copy.quantity = quantity;
        return copy;
    }
}
```

## What the verifier found

The two builds disagree on `shop.Pricing#withQuantity`. The checker found this input, and the verifier replayed it on the JVM against both builds (an entry point under the same recording stubs, a kernel method with its objects made by their constructors):

| Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `withQuantity(q=new Quote(new Money(0), 1), quantity=0)` | `Quote{cents=0, quantity=0}, leaving q=Quote{cents=0, quantity=0}, with result == q` | `Quote{amount=Money{cents=0}, quantity=0}, leaving q=Quote{amount=Money{cents=0}, quantity=0}` |

The domain is `q: a Quote made by its constructor, Quote(amount: Money(cents: long), quantity: int), from any arguments it accepts; in the previous version, a Quote made by its constructor, Quote(cents: long, quantity: int), from the new q's amount.cents and quantity as the correspondence's input equations say (old.q.cents == new.q.amount.cents, old.q.quantity == new.q.quantity), and satisfying them × quantity: int`.

Every part the run checked, nothing written by hand (the entry points under their observation specs, each kernel pair under the correspondence alignment proposed), and what the rerun on the same proof cache took from the first run:

| Part | Kind | Verdict | On the rerun | Why not verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /quotes` | entry point | verified | an exact hit |  |
| `POST /quotes/text` | entry point | unresolved | not a proof | `what the analysis can't see stays unresolved: the old build: a dynamic call site the walk doesn't follow: StringConcatFactory.makeConcatWithConstants in QuotesController.quoteText(long, int) (string concatenation: the string's value isn't modeled); the new build: a dynamic call site the walk doesn't follow: StringConcatFactory.makeConcatWithConstants in QuotesController.quoteText(long, int) (string concatenation: the string's value isn't modeled)` |
| `shop.Pricing#discount` | kernel | verified | an exact hit |  |
| `shop.Pricing#total` | kernel | verified | an exact hit; `Pricing.discount` proved on its own and taken as one function |  |
| `shop.Pricing#withQuantity` | kernel | refuted | an exact hit |  |
| `shop.Money#cents (was shop.Quote#cents)` | kernel | unresolved | not a proof | `class not found in the previous version: shop.Money` |
| `shop.Quote#quantity` | kernel | unresolved | not a proof | `the receiver is made differently in the two versions: this: a Quote made by its constructor, Quote(cents: long, quantity: int), from any arguments it accepts before, this: a Quote made by its constructor, Quote(amount: Money(cents: long), quantity: int), from any arguments it accepts now; a receiver of another construction or other fields is not supported yet` |

Obligations, one per observation of an old entry point: 7 preserved, 1 unresolved. Decisions a person made, by category: approved exclusion 0, domain restriction 0, environment assumption 0, mapping 0, observation change 0.

No question is left for a person.

What the verdicts rest on that nobody decided (assumed, not approved):

- KafkaTemplate.send is a recording stub in both builds: a recorded attempt is the call attempted, with its payload snapshotted at the call, not a delivery or a commit
- every modeled call returns normally, the environment model's only outcome: a failure of a store, broker or client is outside the claim
- QuotesController is made by its constructor with every dependency null and every other argument zero, in both builds: its dependencies are reached only through the modeled calls, and configuration it would be given is the type's default

## Would the existing tests have caught it?

No: every existing unit test passes (`java -ea shop.Tests`, run against the patched code).

## Why it matters

Turning a returned argument into a copy is a common defensive edit, and with a value object in the change it looks harmless: the copy has the same amount and quantity. A comparison of returned values field by field passes. Only a caller that relies on getting back the object it passed, and goes on to change one and read the other, sees the difference.

## Why the verdict is right

The run's kernel observations for a Java API method include the identity relation of the result with each object parameter of the result's class, compared within each version as "holds before iff it holds now", never by object ids across versions. Before, `result == q` holds; after, it doesn't. The copy is made for one item and then given the quantity, so that the constructor's refusal of a quantity below 1 doesn't tell the versions apart first: the result's fields and `q`'s agree on every input, and identity is the only observation refuted.

## What to do

Hand back `q`, as before, or make the copy the intended change and tell its callers.

## Notes

- Checked by `jvmcontract compare`, which build.py runs as the B9 check of the shop app (`run_tool_compare`): the unpatched build against the patched one, twice under one fresh proof cache, the verdict read from the rerun and the page's output from the first run. The verdict is the subject's; the page lists every other part the run checked.
- The joint example of `llm-dlc/loops/foundations.md`'s Phase 5, made an example: the app's sources are the fixture's `before` build (`lib/tests/fixtures/foundations/`), and the patch turns them into its `after` build with the alias-to-copy defect (`defects/alias-to-copy/`) overlaid. `lib/tests/compare.rs` holds `jvmcontract compare` to the same builds inline; this is the same run by build.py, with the app's tests run too.
- Nothing in the run is written by hand. The entry points' external inputs (`cents`, `quantity`) are anchored by their observation specs, so no mapping is involved at the boundary. The kernel's relation between the old and new quotes (`old.q.cents == new.q.amount.cents`, `old.q.quantity == new.q.quantity`) is alignment's proposal, inferred from how the two constructors route their parameters into the fields; it stays *proposed*, its evidence the proof under its claim key, and since nothing external anchors a kernel method's inputs, a proved relation there is reported as proved and not as the intended one.
- What stays unresolved in every example of the set, by name: `POST /quotes/text` (its string concatenation isn't modeled), `Quote#cents` moved to `Money#cents` (a method of a class the old build doesn't have) and the instance method `Quote#quantity` (the regression check takes static methods, or a record's over its primitive components).
- Run inline on 2026-11-07 (JDK 25.0.5), `jvmcontract compare` on the app compiled unpatched and patched, as build.py compiles it, and on the fixture's builds, with the same verdicts (the times are the fixture's): `Pricing#withQuantity` refuted on `identity:result==q` alone, on `withQuantity(new Quote(new Money(0), 1), 0)`, replayed on a JVM with the objects' identities; `POST /quotes`, `total` and `discount` verified. 0.4 s cold, 0.2 s warm.
- `POST /quotes` is an exact hit of 190's proof when run under 190's cache, rightly: the defect changes only `withQuantity`, which the route doesn't reach, so the rewritten builds of the route are 190's (`lib/tests/compare.rs`). Here each example runs under a fresh cache, so it is proved and then reused on the rerun.
- The app's tests pass on this version: none keeps the quote it passed.
